title: Pullback image of products by recursive ideal powers
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $Y$, $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module, and $n\ge 0$. Let $T=f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $I=J\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and use the recursive module-subobject powers and ideal-module products of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Then the image subobject of $T(J^nG\hookrightarrow G)$ equals the image subobject of $I^n T(G)\hookrightarrow T(G)$ inside $T(G)$. At $n=0$ the power is the full structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0887, displayed quotient computation in the proof; checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0887

proof.text: The recursive power inclusion is monic: at zero it is the identity, at one the ideal inclusion, and each later inclusion is a composite of the image inclusion of a product with the preceding power inclusion. On each affine open the positive-power section range is J(U)^n by the ideal-times-quasi-coherent affine-sections theorem. The section range of (J^n).toModulesι is the same ideal by range_toModulesι_app and ideal_pow. At n=0 both ranges are the whole structure sheaf. Reuse Scheme.subobject_le_of_affine_range from ClosedImmersionIdealPowerImage (available through proof-only import all) in both directions. These equal ranges imply equality of subobjects: the affine basis detects zero morphisms by sheaf separatedness, so each inclusion followed by the other cokernel projection is zero. Lift through the kernel of that projection and invert the abelian image factorization of the monomorphism to obtain both subobject inequalities. Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk gives an isomorphism from the recursive power to (J^n).toModules over the structure sheaf.

An isomorphism e between two modules over the structure sheaf, commuting with their inclusions, gives an isomorphism between their ideal-module products with any module F. Whiskering e with F is an isomorphism and identifies the two multiplication maps. Precomposition with an isomorphism leaves imageSubobject unchanged. Equality of the resulting image subobjects gives a product isomorphism commuting with the product inclusions. Apply this to the power comparison on Y and on X. All of this is proved locally in the module, with no remaining proof hole.

The already-proved upstream Scheme.IdealSheafData.comap_pow gives (J^n).comap f = (J.comap f)^n for every natural n, including zero (WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Functorial.lean). Apply modulePullbackIdealProductImage to the ideal-data power J^n and the given quasi-coherent G; it equates the pulled-back image of the product by J^n with the product by its extended ideal.

Rewrite the source product inclusion using the commuting product isomorphism on Y. Functoriality of tensorPullback and invariance of imageSubobject under precomposition by an isomorphism identify its pulled-back image with the image for J^n. Use the one-power equality, rewrite the extended ideal using the power identity, and apply the commuting product isomorphism on X backwards. This gives precisely the required equality for every natural n, including zero. No extra finiteness or nonemptiness hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback), quotient computation; reduced to the existing one-power image theorem using the affine recursive-power formula, upstream comap_pow, and isomorphisms of image inclusions; shortened by P2 second reading. lean.statement: theorem modulePullbackIdealPowerProductImage {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G : Y.Modules) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℕ) : imageSubobject ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).map (Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι n).2 G)) = imageSubobject (Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower (J.comap f).toModulesι n).2 ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).obj G))
